response:
Diagnosis after six rounds. The archive has converged on a clear structure: an *enterprise-scaled* valuation gate multiplied by a signed, standardized accrual-quality leg. SalesToEnterpriseGatedAccrualQuality is now the best entry on every metric jointly (FMB 2.48, FF5 alpha +4.4% with t = 4.22, Sharpe 0.354, coverage 0.104), with EVYieldGatedAccrualQuality close behind. Three further lessons: (i) cash-flow-statement accrual measurement buys alpha but destroys the cross-sectional slope and costs 1.5pp of coverage (FMB 0.34), so I stop pursuing it; (ii) hard INDICATOR gating creates a degenerate zero spike that cost the reversal-completion leg its alpha when moved under the EV gate (2.2% → 1.0%), so the stage-of-cycle idea needs a smooth weight instead; (iii) leverage weighting produced the strongest FMB slope in the archive (3.37) but a *negative* alpha, i.e. it injects a low-leverage factor tilt — the asymmetry (positive-part accruals) is worth keeping, the leverage multiplier is not.

This batch consolidates around the revenue-to-enterprise gate: refining the gate itself (industry-relative, dual-gate), refining the accrual leg it is paired with (asymmetric positive-part, revenue-commensurate deflator, smooth stage-of-cycle weight), plus one continuous-scale construction that puts the accrual correction inside an enterprise multiple rather than using a gate at all.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: PeerRelativeRevenueMultipleGatedAccrual
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Revenue-to-enterprise-value is mechanically determined by industry margin structure — a grocery distributor always looks cheap on revenue and a software firm never does — so cheapness on revenue is only informative relative to industry peers, and the accrual test should be applied to firms that are genuinely cheap for their business model.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The revenue-multiple gate is the archive's best-performing valuation leg, but its cross-sectional rank is contaminated by a large industry component that dilutes exactly the conditioning it is meant to provide; ranking within industry concentrates the gate on firm-specific cheapness. This is an economic correction to the gate's interpretation rather than a normalization tweak, and it should lift both the FMB slope (less industry noise in the gate) and Sharpe (fewer unintended sector bets).
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DualEnterpriseGateAccrualQuality
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che)), RATIO(ebitda, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che)))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness on revenue and cheapness on operating profit identify overlapping but distinct populations — the first catches firms with temporarily compressed margins, the second firms whose existing cash generation is underpriced — and a firm cheap on both dimensions is the most reliable place to apply the accrual test.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two enterprise gates were the archive's top two performers with similar alpha but different composition, which suggests each contains gate-specific measurement noise that averaging can remove; a combined rank also keeps firms with temporarily negative EBITDA in the gate through their revenue multiple. This is a substantive robustness gain in the conditioning variable rather than another accrual-leg variant, and it should improve portfolio stability, where the gated family has been weakest.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: RevenueGatedIncomeIncreasingAccrualOnly
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(MUL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), 0))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Only income-increasing accruals create an obligation to reverse; income-decreasing accruals are conservatism and should earn no reward, so among firms cheap on revenue the short leg should be built purely from those inflating current earnings while the long leg holds all firms with no accrual inflation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The levered asymmetric penalty produced the strongest cross-sectional slope in the entire archive (FMB 3.37) but a negative alpha, which localizes the problem in the leverage multiplier's low-leverage factor tilt rather than in the asymmetry; removing leverage and keeping the positive-part restriction should retain the slope while restoring the enterprise gate's alpha. It also directly tests whether the accrual side of the value-trap story is one-sided, a question the symmetric legs cannot answer.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: RevenueGatedRevenueScaledAccrual
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), sale)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: When cheapness is measured per dollar of revenue, the matching accounting-quality question is how much accrual accounting was required per dollar of that same revenue; asset scaling instead mixes in capital intensity, which is irrelevant to whether revenue is being collected.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The deflator has never been tested commensurately with the gate: sales-deflated accruals were only tried under an earnings-yield gate, where they gave a strong alpha (3.4%, t=3.2) but almost no slope, plausibly because the gate and leg measured different things. Matching both to revenue makes the composite internally consistent and isolates the deflator choice against the current best signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: WorkingCapitalChargedEnterpriseYield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))
HYPOTHESIS: The correct enterprise multiple charges operating profit for the working capital the business had to absorb to produce it, so a firm is cheap only if the profit remaining after that charge is large relative to total enterprise value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every enterprise-gated signal in the archive uses a [0,1] rank gate that flattens most of the cross-section and has repeatedly produced FMB t-stats of 0.3–2.6, whereas the archive's continuous-scale signals reliably delivered FMB t-stats above 3 but only ever used equity-market deflators, which are HML-collinear. This construction is continuous *and* enterprise-scaled, embedding the accrual correction in the numerator, so it is the natural test of whether the FMB weakness of the winning family is caused by the gate's functional form rather than its economics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RevenueGatedSmoothReversalStage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)), RANK(LAG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 1))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm's prospects depend on where it sits in the accrual cycle, and the informativeness of this year's working-capital release scales continuously with how much was accumulated last year rather than switching on at zero.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The stage-of-cycle mechanism gave the best FMB slope of the gated family under a book-to-market gate (2.75) but lost most of its alpha when moved under the enterprise gate (2.2% → 1.0%), and the diagnosed cause is the hard INDICATOR, which assigns exactly zero to every firm without a prior build-up and leaves the standardized leg dominated by a degenerate spike. Replacing the indicator with the cross-sectional rank of last year's accrual produces a smooth, non-degenerate weight that keeps the same economics with a well-behaved distribution.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE PeerRelativeRevenueMultipleGatedAccrual---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a one-operator normalization swap (RANK → IND_RANK) on the archive's existing best signal SalesToEnterpriseGatedAccrualQuality, and while industry-neutralizing a margin-driven revenue multiple is economically sensible, it is the kind of cosmetic variant the objective explicitly discourages absent a diagnosed failure it repairs.

---CRITIQUE DualEnterpriseGateAccrualQuality---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Averaging the two enterprise-yield gates from two already-evaluated signals against an identical accrual leg is an ensemble of prior results rather than a new mechanism, and since sale/EV and ebitda/EV share the same denominator and are highly correlated, the outcome will almost mechanically interpolate between the two known alphas.

---CRITIQUE RevenueGatedIncomeIncreasingAccrualOnly---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The positive-part restriction is a defensible decomposition test that isolates whether the negative alpha of LeveredIncomeIncreasingAccrualTrap came from the leverage multiplier or the asymmetry, and the expression's sign logic is coherent, though the hard indicator leaves roughly half the cross-section stacked at exactly zero — the same degeneracy this batch's own sixth proposal complains about.

---CRITIQUE RevenueGatedRevenueScaledAccrual---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Swapping the accrual deflator from assets to sales under the existing best gate is a single-parameter robustness variant whose "commensurate deflator" justification is rhetorical rather than economic — the gate's denominator is enterprise value, not sales, so nothing is actually made internally consistent — and the archive already shows this leg's behavior under a different gate.

---CRITIQUE WorkingCapitalChargedEnterpriseYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: This is the only proposal that changes functional form rather than a component, embedding the accrual charge in the numerator to produce a continuous enterprise-scaled yield, and it directly tests the stated diagnosis that the gated family's weak FMB slopes come from the flattened [0,1] rank gate — though the reviewer should note it sits close to published cash-flow-to-enterprise-value and cash-based-profitability measures, so a high-alpha result may be rediscovery rather than novelty.

---CRITIQUE RevenueGatedSmoothReversalStage---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The stated diagnosis is internally inconsistent — the INDICATOR was identical in both the book-to-market and enterprise-gated reversal signals, so it cannot explain an alpha difference that arose purely from changing the gate — and the smoothing itself is a functional-form tweak on an already-evaluated mechanism rather than a new economic claim.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: EnterpriseYieldGatedDepreciationAdequacy
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(dp, at))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The EBITDA multiple's specific blind spot is that it ignores capital consumption, so for firms that look cheap on EBITDA the decisive accounting question is depreciation adequacy: a peer-abnormally high depreciation charge means the profit being capitalized will never reach shareholders, making the apparent cheapness an artifact of the multiple's construction.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is not a normalization swap but a new claim about *which* accrual matters for *which* multiple: depreciation is the largest non-cash charge and is precisely the item the enterprise gate excludes, so pairing them tests a mechanism no archived signal addresses. Note the sign is deliberately the opposite of the archived DepreciationConservatismValue, where high depreciation was rewarded because net income was already charged for it — the reversal is forced by the gate's construction, which makes the two results jointly interpretable rather than redundant.
REASONING: Industry adjustment is essential because dp/at mostly reflects capital intensity, and coverage should exceed the archive norm since no differencing is required in the accrual leg.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: RevenueGatedCollectionEfficiencyDecay
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A single year's accrual build-up is mostly cyclical noise, but a multi-year upward drift in receivables-and-inventory per dollar of revenue is evidence of structural decay — lengthening collection periods and slower inventory turns — and a firm cheap on revenue with decaying collection efficiency is a business in decline rather than a mispriced asset.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The archive has tested accrual levels, one-year changes, three-year means, five-year volatility, five-year own-history rank and distance-from-peak, but never a fitted multi-year *slope*, which is the only statistic that distinguishes persistent directional deterioration from mean-reverting fluctuation. The economic claim is new and specific to the revenue-multiple gate: cheapness on revenue is only a bargain if that revenue is still being converted to cash at a stable or improving rate.
REASONING: The five-year window costs some coverage relative to one-year legs, so I will read the result against the archive's other multi-year signals rather than the one-year benchmarks.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: RevenueGatedAccrualWithoutCashBuffer
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(MUL(MUL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), 0)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, at))))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: An accrual reversal is an accounting event for a cash-rich firm but a financing event for a cash-poor one, because the unwind of receivables and inventory has to be funded; the value trap is therefore the joint state of cheap price, income-increasing accruals, and no liquidity buffer to absorb the reversal.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This adds a genuinely new conditioning dimension — the balance-sheet liquidity cushion — rather than another deflator, and it is deliberately built to avoid the failure of the earlier leverage-weighted version: the INDICATOR restricts amplification to income-increasing accruals, so a cash-poor firm with conservative accruals receives exactly zero penalty and cannot enter the long leg on liquidity grounds alone. Using the cross-sectional rank of cash scarcity keeps the weight bounded in [0,1] so a few cash-hoarding firms cannot dominate the standardized leg.
REASONING: Because both the amplifier and the penalty vanish for conservative reporters, the short leg is specifically illiquid, accrual-inflated, cheap firms — the archetype the economic story names.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: RevenueGatedUnjustifiedWorkingCapitalInvestment
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), MUL(GROWTH(sale, 1), LAG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), at), 1)))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Working capital should grow in proportion to revenue, so the benchmark for normal accrual investment is last year's working-capital intensity scaled by this year's revenue growth; only the excess over that benchmark represents receivables and inventory accumulating without corresponding business expansion, which is the accounting signature of a value trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This implements an explicit expectation model for normal accruals — the symbolic analogue of the Jones-model fitted value — instead of the crude industry demeaning that made the earlier discretionary-accrual attempt fail (alpha 0.2%, t 0.14), and it is continuous with no degenerate mass point. It also sharpens the interaction with the revenue-multiple gate: a firm cheap on revenue that is investing in working capital faster than its revenue justifies is exactly the case where cheapness reflects deteriorating fundamentals rather than mispricing.
REASONING: All inputs are broadly populated balance-sheet and revenue items over two years, so coverage should stay near the archive norm of 0.10.
